intent: Give assistive technology text the screen does not show.
typical_uses: The name of an icon-only link or of a custom control that has no label prop
A table caption that the surrounding heading already shows visually

dont_use_when.situation: Text that should be hidden from everyone

instead.target: The `sr-only` class of the kit's utilities.css

dont_use_when.situation: The name of an icon-only Button
The name of a status dot shown without a label

invariants.text: The box is absolutely positioned, one pixel square, clipped with `clip-path: inset(50%)`, without padding or border, and does not wrap, the same declarations as the kit's internal `.srOnly` copies and the `sr-only` utility.
The text stays in the accessibility tree and names its container.

anti_patterns.dont: Hide text with `display: none` to keep it for screen readers
anti_patterns.do_instead: Use VisuallyHidden; `display: none` removes it from the tree too

render.states: render replaces the span with one the caller supplies
render.because: useRender's render prop takes an element or a function that receives the props to spread (VisuallyHidden passes no state of its own), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property. It is for the element, such as `render={<caption />}`.

bad.title: A visible label hidden for no reason
bad.why: Sighted users need the label too, and the hidden text does not name the input; use Label with `htmlFor`.
